questions.prompt: Where do the animals in the listening story live?
steps: Identify the setting of Mr Lion’s leadership.
The meeting and changes take place in a forest.

questions.prompt: Which animals mocked Mr Lion’s speech?
steps: Separate supporters who cheered from opponents who resisted changes.
The passage describes the opponents as conservative.

questions.prompt: Why did Mr Lion give small animals power?
steps: Identify the hardship experienced by the smaller animals.
His change benefited the group that had been suffering most.
questions.answer: A — They were the most disadvantaged animals.

questions.prompt: What had the forest become after five years?
steps: Follow the sequence from his first changes to the later result.
The place developed into a large town.

questions.prompt: What did greedy animals do if they could not change their lifestyles?
steps: The story contrasts adapting to change with leaving.
Those who would not adapt moved away from the forest.

questions.prompt: My sister ___ very good English in 2008.
steps: In 2008 is a finished past-time expression.
Use the simple past form spoke.

questions.prompt: My cat has been ___ for two years.
steps: After has been, the blank describes a continuing state.
Dead is an adjective; died is the event and death is a noun.

questions.prompt: I was ___ my homework when you called.
steps: Was introduces an action in progress in the past.
Use was + -ing form.

questions.prompt: Mrs Daudi ___ your friend for years now.
steps: For years now expresses a situation continuing into the present.
A singular subject takes has been.

questions.prompt: ___ Mrs Mawazo teach English these days?
steps: This is a present-simple question about a singular person.
Use Does + subject + base verb teach.

questions.prompt: The book belongs to ___.
steps: After the preposition to, use an object pronoun.
Him is the object form referring to the male owner.

questions.prompt: The man ___ coat is brown is my uncle.
steps: The relative word expresses possession of the coat.
Whose means belonging to whom.

questions.prompt: I ___ Sabasaba Day to Heroes Day.
steps: The comparison pattern is prefer X to Y.
The subject I takes the base form prefer.

questions.prompt: Mwera came ___ of the shop.
steps: Leaving an enclosed place is coming out of it.
Complete the phrase out of.

questions.prompt: The old man was walking ___ the river.
steps: The intended route follows the length of the river.
Along describes movement beside a line or feature.

questions.prompt: Which is not a preposition of movement: behind, through, out of, onto, around?
steps: Through, out of, onto and around can describe paths of movement.
Behind normally identifies a position relative to something.

questions.prompt: How ___ cars did you see?
steps: Cars is a plural countable noun.
Use many to ask about their number.

questions.prompt: Add a tag to She doesn’t work with us.
steps: A negative statement takes a positive tag.
Repeat does and the subject she.

questions.prompt: Change The camera was broken by Tom into active voice.
steps: Make the agent Tom the subject.
Keep the simple past tense and use broke.

questions.prompt: Ask your teacher for permission to visit the washroom.
steps: Use a polite request for permission.
May I is the standard form offered in the choices.
questions.answer: E — Please, may I go to the washroom?

questions.prompt: What suffix makes job mean without a job?
steps: The suffix -less means without.
Attach it to job to form jobless.

questions.prompt: Find the root of uncomfortable.
steps: Remove the prefix un- and suffix -able.
The remaining root is comfort.

questions.prompt: Choose the closest opposite of truth.
steps: Truth concerns what is real or honest.
Of the choices, dishonesty expresses a lack of truthfulness.
questions.tip: Falsehood or a lie would be more direct opposites, but neither appears in the options.

questions.prompt: Which word is closest to strong?
steps: The context describes physical strength.
Powerful expresses similar physical ability.

questions.prompt: What is a person recording debate points called?
steps: Recording proceedings is a secretarial duty.
Choose secretary rather than the chair, speaker or timekeeper.

questions.prompt: Name a variety of food supplying what is needed for good health.
steps: The description concerns adequate variety and proportions of nutrients.
That is called a balanced diet.

questions.prompt: What occupation makes wooden chairs in a workshop?
steps: Identify the material and product: wooden furniture.
The person doing this work is a carpenter.

questions.prompt: Who repairs a car that has broken down?
steps: Repairing vehicle machinery is mechanical work.
A mechanic performs that job.

questions.prompt: How do you greet someone you meet at 8:18 p.m.?
steps: This is an evening greeting when meeting someone.
Good night is normally used when leaving or going to bed.

questions.prompt: Toni was sad because he was ___ to perform well.
steps: The structure is unable to + verb.
It expresses lack of ability and explains his disappointment.

questions.prompt: What good quality makes Bauta a wonderful friend?
steps: Choose a positive quality rather than a negative habit.
Kindness describes being considerate and helpful.

questions.prompt: A grandfather with no teeth is ___.
steps: The suffix -less means without.
Tooth + less = toothless.

questions.prompt: A good student should avoid ___ behaviour.
steps: Avoid concerns something undesirable.
Bad is the adjective fitting the intended contrast.

questions.prompt: What form should be used for more than one item of furniture?
steps: Furniture is an uncountable noun in standard English.
It stays furniture; use pieces of furniture when counting.
questions.tip: Do not add -s to form furnitures.

questions.prompt: I packed sweaters but did not wear them because it was ___.
steps: Sweaters are normally worn for warmth.
The context implies the weather was too warm for them.

questions.prompt: Order the letter part: 23 July 2022.
steps: A personal letter gives the sender’s address first.
The date follows the address, making it the second part.

questions.prompt: Order the letter part: I am writing to remind you of my birthday.
steps: This is the body of the letter.
Place it after the address, date and greeting.

questions.prompt: Order the letter part: Dear mother,
steps: This is the greeting or salutation.
Place it after the address and date, before the body.

questions.prompt: Order the letter part: P.O. Box 4421, Kokoto.
steps: This is the sender’s address.
Place it at the beginning.

questions.prompt: Order the letter part: Your son, Mfalme.
steps: This is the closing and writer’s name.
It follows the message.

questions.prompt: What is the king’s wife called?
steps: The daughter is a princess and the father is a king.
The royal title for the king’s wife is queen.

questions.prompt: Who failed to marry the princess?
steps: The king’s condition required returning with her alive.
The earlier brave rescuers did not survive their attempts.
questions.answer: The brave men who attempted the rescue before Maguvu.

questions.prompt: What might have happened if robbers caught Maguvu during the rescue?
steps: Use the fate of earlier rescuers to make a supported prediction.
The robbers had killed men who tried to rescue the princess.
questions.tip: This is an inference, not an event that actually happened in the passage.

questions.prompt: Why are the robbers described as bad people?
steps: Identify their harmful actions rather than merely repeat the label bad.
They killed the king’s wife, abducted his daughter and killed rescuers.
questions.answer: They harmed others by murder and kidnapping.

questions.prompt: Why did the king promise marriage to the rescuer?
steps: The king wanted his daughter returned alive.
The promise was a reward intended to motivate a successful rescue.
questions.answer: To encourage someone to rescue his daughter and bring her home alive.

summaries.Section A — Listening: Track setting, opposing groups, reasons and consequences. Answer what the passage actually says.
summaries.Section A — Grammar and vocabulary: Use tense markers and grammatical function. Learn fixed expressions, word roots and suffixes rather than memorising option letters.
summaries.Section B — Letter writing: The complete order is 39 → 36 → 38 → 37 → 40: address, date, greeting, body and closing.
summaries.Section C — Comprehension: Use stated actions as evidence. For prediction questions, explain what the earlier events make likely.

references.title: NECTA: PSLE 2022 English analysis and listening passage
